metas.name: Brick Meta - B-Type Brick
metas.note:
The B-type brick can be recognized by its three deep horizontal slots.

It is especially common across northeastern Brazil, including Ceará, Rio Grande do Norte, Paraíba, Pernambuco, Sergipe, eastern Piauí, and western Bahia. It is also frequently found in Acre, Manaus, eastern Pará, São Paulo, Mato Grosso do Sul, western Mato Grosso, western Minas Gerais, and Tocantins.

Be careful in transition zones, where both A-type and B-type bricks may appear in the same area.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil: The Brick Meta, by @XyuTwo

metas.name: Brick Meta - C-Type Brick
metas.note:
The C-type brick can be recognized by its four deep horizontal slots.

This type is considerably rarer than the A-type and B-type bricks. It is found mainly in southern Bahia, Rio de Janeiro, and some surrounding areas.

Because of its rarity, a clearly visible C-type brick can provide strong regional information, although other clues should still be considered.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil: The Brick Meta, by @XyuTwo

metas.name: Brick Meta - D-Type Brick
metas.note:
The D-type brick has very fine cracks, shallow slots, or slight horizontal ridges. From a distance, these markings may look like faint lines, and some bricks may appear almost completely smooth.

Unlike the other types, D-type bricks can be found throughout Brazil. They are especially common in large cities and in areas such as Belém, central Minas Gerais, central Goiás, São Paulo, and the eastern coast between João Pessoa and Rio de Janeiro.

Since D-type bricks can coexist with other brick types, prioritize a clearly identifiable A-type or B-type brick when both are present.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil: The Brick Meta, by @XyuTwo

metas.name: Brick Meta - E-Type Brick
metas.note:
The E-type brick has multiple deep horizontal slots, usually six or more.

It may resemble some versions of the D-type brick, but its slots are generally deeper, clearer, and less numerous than the extremely fine ridges found on D-type bricks.

This type is uncommon but regionally useful, as it is mainly associated with central Bahia, northern Alagoas, and northern Sergipe. Only use this clue when the slots are clearly visible.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil: The Brick Meta, by @XyuTwo

metas.name: Brick Meta - Single-Line Brick
metas.note:
The single-line brick can be recognized by its single visible horizontal slot or groove.

This brick is not a useful regional clue. It is widespread across Brazil and does not follow a consistent geographic pattern.

Treat it as non-diagnostic: do not use it to determine the state or region. Prioritize clearly identifiable A-type, B-type, C-type, D-type, or E-type bricks and other surrounding clues instead.

This type is included as a negative clue: seeing it should not influence your regional guess.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil: The Brick Meta, by @XyuTwo

metas.name: Brick Meta: A-Type
metas.note:
The A-type brick can be recognized by its two deep horizontal slots.

It is the dominant brick type across southern Brazil, especially in Paraná, Santa Catarina, and Rio Grande do Sul. It is also common in Rondônia, Roraima, Amapá, western Pará, Maranhão, western Piauí, southern Bahia, Tocantins, and parts of Goiás.

Some exceptions and transition zones exist, particularly where A-type and B-type bricks overlap.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil: The Brick Meta, by @XyuTwo
